abstract:
Human-AI collaboration is increasingly relevant in consequential areas where AI recommendations support human discretion. However, human-AI teams’ effectiveness, capability, and fairness highly depend on human perceptions of AI. Positive fairness perceptions have been shown to foster trust and acceptance of AI recommendations. Yet, work on confirmation bias highlights that humans selectively adhere to AI recommendations that align with their expectations and beliefs—despite those recommendations not being necessarily correct or fair. This raises the question of whether confirmation bias also transfers to the alignment of gender bias between human and AI decisions. In our study, we examine how gender bias alignment and the presence of explanations accompanying the AI recommendation influence fairness perceptions, human self-confidence, and reliance on the AI system. Findings from two 2
                    
                      \(\times\)
                    
                    2 between-subjects studies underscore the relationship between gender-bias alignment, fairness perceptions, and reliance, demonstrating that merely constructing a “formally fair” AI system is insufficient for optimal human–AI collaboration. Ultimately, AI recommendations are likely to be overridden when the system's biases do not align with those of its users.

ur.ai_reason: 人机团队公平感知用户研究，核心HCI实验设计
ur.tldr: 研究人机协作中AI与人类决策者的性别偏见一致性如何影响用户对公平性的感知及对AI建议的依赖程度。通过两项2×2被试间实验，发现即使AI系统在形式上满足公平性标准，当其偏见方向与用户自身不一致时，用户倾向于推翻AI建议；偏见对齐显著调节公平感知、自我信心与依赖行为。

title: Fairness in the Eye of the Beholder: How Gender Bias Alignment Influences Fairness Perceptions and Reliance in Human–AI Teams
title_zh: 旁观者眼中的公平：性别偏见对齐如何影响人机团队中的公平感知与依赖
